headline: Sustainability| Livelihoods| Public Policy| Development research| CSR
about:
A strong believer in inclusive development through sustainable use of resources, equitable benefit sharing, and responsible production and consumption.

Development research helps me earn my bread and butter. My major involvement lies in conducting research studies to identify gaps and opportunities for promoting nature-based solutions.

These days, trying to find my footing in public policy, carbon financing, and the equity market.

experience.description: Worked in various livelihood generation projects focusing on promotion of sustainable value chains and producer enterprises. Major contributions are through conducting- research to inform in project designing, impact evaluation studies, value chain analysis, and business feasibility studies.

Conducted various research studies and consulting assignments mainly around sustainable agriculture, climate change adaptation, rural livelihoods and nutrition.

Worked extensively in the organic farming sector to help prepare implementation strategies forclients like GIZ and Welthungerhilfe. Also, supported FPOs to prepare and adopt viable business plans
around agricultural and forest-based commodities.

As a team member of research teams, I have been closely involved in developing research tools, conducting secondary and field level research, data analysis and report preparation. 

As a member of a growing management consultancy, I have also been involved in business development activities by creating proposals and concept notes.

As a part of the state project management team, contributed in implemention of three livelihoods projects in 11 districts of Odisha.

Developed Detailed Project Report (DPR) and Project Implementation Plan (PIP) for sustainable valuechain interventions on Medicinal Plants and Tasar Sericulture under Mahila Kisan SashaktikaranPariyojana (MKSP) in Odisha.

Contributed in forming community institutions and capacitated them on sustainable sourcingprotocols, primary value addition techniques and market access through grassroots level trainingprograms.
Study to understand the community perception on climatic events and wildlife residing in the fringe of the Protected Areas along river Brahmaputra in Assam.

I was involved as a Research Associate for conducting scoping studies in 4 tea estates to identify the potential access points and understand the demand and spending pattern among the tea garden workers through FGDs.

Conduct studies to inform the design of the project on three thematic areas: 
Livelihoods and climate change analysis, 
Market access and income generation, and
Social, Gender and institution analysis.

As part of the qualitative research team, I was responsible to collect data from Farmers and Farmer Groups on their existing agricultural practices and their vulnerability towards changing climatic events.

projects.title: Value Chain intervention and market linkage of Tasar Sericulture based livelihoods in Odisha
projects.description:
This project was commissioned by the Government of India to increase the household level income of 5220 Tasar Rearers in two districts of Odisha by creating backward linkages through scientific interventions and convergence with Department of Sericulture for improved marketing support.

Coordinate with project stakeholders, develop Detailed Project Report and Project Implementation Plan. Conduct capacity building programs for district and block level officials. Monitoring and evaluation of the project activities by creating KPIs and trackers and manage the MKSP MIS.

projects.title: Value chain intervention and market linkage of medicinal plant species in Odisha
projects.description:
This project was commissioned by the Government of India under the Mahila Kisan Sashaktiran Pariyojana (MKSP) to enhance the income capacity of 9000 rural women farmers/collectors in six districts of Odisha by promoting sustainable harvesting, collective cultivation and Farmer Producers Organizations (FPO) of 7 Medicinal Plants species.

Coordinate with project stakeholders, develop Detailed Project Report and Project Implementation Plan. Conduct capacity building programs for district and block level officials. Monitoring and evaluation of the project activities by creating KPIs and trackers and manage the MKSP MIS.

headline: Product Activation & Customer Success at PwC
topSkills: Agile Project Management • Customer Success • Go-to-Market Strategy • Customer Segmentation Strategy • Customer Lifecycle Management
about:
Delivering exceptional customer experiences has been at the heart of my career for over 8 years. At PwC, my role as a Product Activation & Customer Success Manager centers on maximizing customer value through strategy and innovation in AI transformation products. Creating go-to-market plans with a foundation in Agile methodologies and an array of tools like Gainsight, Pendo and Sprinklr my focus is on accelerating digital delivery that aligns with client goals and enables upsell, cross-sell and renewals. Creating go-to-mat commitment to customer satisfaction is evidenced by our meticulously tracked metrics, such as time to value and NPS.

The hands-on experience from my previous role at Morningstar has honed my skills in customer segmentation and lifecycle marketing, directly contributing to enhanced acquisition, adoption and retention. Collaboratively leading cross-functional teams, I've developed and implemented playbooks and processes that not only meet but exceed stakeholder expectations. This has established me as a trusted advisor who enables clients to thrive in an increasingly digital landscape.

experience.description: As Product Activation & Customer Success Manager for workforce transformation SaaS products, I manage enterprise customer accounts with a focus on retention, adoption, and growth, building playbooks and processes to enhance customer satisfaction by tracking time to value and NPS. Leveraging Agile methodologies, I accelerate the delivery of high-quality digital services, improving the client experience. I develop trusted advisor relationships with key stakeholders, ensuring success plans aligned with their business goals, while facilitating technical and strategic workshops to drive consensus and actionable outcomes. Through multiple client touch points and using tools such as Gainsight, Pendo and SFDC, I identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, collaborate with internal teams to enhance customer value, and track key milestones to provide executive-level insights.

In my role as a Product Marketing Manager, I owned the strategy and execution of lifecycle marketing, creating initiatives for each stage of the customer journey. By leveraging user behavior, activity data, research, and industry-specific insights, I developed customer segmentation and personalization strategies for email campaigns. I partnered with analytics, product, and marketing teams to optimize channels and drive retention, while building hypothesis-based tests to refine segmentation, channel, and messaging for key results.

As a member of the Bosch Auto Service team, I led initiatives to transition the automotive aftermarket industry into the digital realm. By crafting and executing lead generation and digital analytics strategies, I enhanced operational efficiency and streamlined the partner experience within the program. Through consultative client meetings and comprehensive success plans, I drove program adoption and identified opportunities for developing new digital products. I also led an offshore development team to bring these opportunities to fruition. Throughout the client lifecycle—from acquisition to retention—I fostered strong relationships and implemented tailored strategies that delivered effective solutions to automotive workshops, ultimately boosting network engagement.

As a digital strategist, I implemented a digital transformation plan that introduced new tools for social listening and internal client data management. By focusing on data analysis and insights, I created and executed digital campaigns that significantly boosted conversions and lead generation. Additionally, I consulted with and guided internal teams to enhance product development based on these insights, while leading special projects to develop new digital products.

I began my career at Bosch in Brazil, where I supported the Latin America sales team and concentrated on projects for new revenue streams. After my transfer to the U.S. market, I created and implemented strategies to enhance brand awareness and in-store visibility. I also led the development of a new segment targeting a fresh audience for the company. In this role, I also introduced user acquisition strategies into the overall marketing plan and managed the digital advertising processes, including performance analysis, to ensure effective execution and measurable results.

headline: Data Risk & Privacy Director - PwC
about:
Katy ​(CIPP/US, CIPP/E) is a Director with PwC’s Data Risk & Privacy group, working with global and domestic clients to understand and improve their current capability to comply with various regulations as part of a holistic data privacy and security strategy. Katy has diverse legal and data protection experience including regulatory compliance, policy management, information security, third party management, and training. 

Katy leads breach analytics and notification projects, supporting the definition, identification, and quantification of sensitive data for the purpose of notifying individuals, business partners, and regulators. Katy leads PwC's Privacy Deals team, providing data privacy expertise in M&A due diligence and pre/post close support and IPO readiness, complimenting the Cyber Deals services. Katy also focuses on healthcare privacy and risk management, supporting  traditional health and pharma organizations and healthcare adjacent companies address new privacy and digital health challenges. She manages global and domestic projects, executing assessments, defining strategy, and implementing program processes and tech aligned to GDPR, US State Privacy laws, HIPAA, NIST, and ISO requirements. Her experience provides clients with an understanding of what is required for a defensible privacy compliance program and how to achieve it.

Prior to joining PwC, Katy worked in healthcare compliance and practiced law, including commercial litigation and transactional health law. She has a Juris Doctorate and Health Law Certificate from Loyola University Chicago School of Law (Chicago, IL) and a Bachelors in Sociology from University the of Kansas (Lawrence, KS).

David is clear on his goals and his career path. I am confidant that he will be a Partner in a top-tier public accounting firm in the not-too-distant future. He carries my highest recommendation!

about:
I have extensive experience with in technical architecture, infrastructure architecture, system administration across platforms (Unix, Linux, and Windows), as well as a developer background across a range of platforms.

I am currently focusing on work involving infrastructure and technical architecture, typically with the IBM WebSphere and Tivoli suites.

Specialties: Middleware infrastructure architecture and administration, technical architecture, enterprise application monitoring design and administration, performance tuning, web development, system automation scripting.

experience.description: My primary responsibilities at American Express were to support production services. I was expected to have extensive knowledge of all applications and processes around all of the systems I worked with, and to use that knowledge to ensure that all system SLAs and customer CTQs are met. I acted as an escalation point and subject matter expert for these systems, ensuring immediate restoration of service after outages. Additionally, I reviewed and certify project plans, IT estimates, requirements, and design documents prior to release into the production environment. The systems that I was primarily responsible for were the enterprise level applications that provide services to thousands of clients. I maintained the infrastructure environment that these systems operated in, tuning and updating as needed.

I provide technical expertise to a variety of enterprise level applications in use by our business. This requires many different functions including: certifying project plans, IT estimates, requirements, development and testing plans, and deployment. In the majority of these tasks, I use Project Management and Six Sigma tools.

I am also responsible for maintaining service level CTQs, acting as an escalation point in the event of an emergency, and restoring service immediately upon any system failures.

This position requires advanced knowledge of Windows and Solaris administration, middleware technologies administration, monitoring software capabilities, and the ability to program various languages.

Windows system administration, including  Active Directory and  Microsoft Exchange, as well as all system backups using Veritas software and SpectraLogic robotic tape systems.

Linux system administration, including Asterisk VoIP, snort IDS, SmoothWall Firewall, and  a PXES thin client solution for a remote center. Monitored all systems and networks using  Hyperic HQ, MRTG, and Nagios.

ITN International provides data and lead retrieval services to a variety of companies for use during their sales meetings, trade shows, or other corporate events.

I traveled extensively to off site events and setup networks of up to 100 windows based workstations and servers. Extensive work with computer hardware, network hardware, and multiple types of PDA equipment. Data gathered by the networks was maintained in MS SQL servers.

projects.title: Cities of Opportunity feature story: "Cities as a Solution to an Aging World"
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Price Waterhouse Management Consultants
projects.description: Researching, interviewing, and writing an article about urbanism and aging demographics in a global context.  Against a backdrop of demographic mega-trends--low fertility rates combined with looming elder population projections--many have suggested that an unsustainable economic crisis is on the horizon. This article acknowledges the seriousness of the demographic trends but finds many options that suggest a manageable path. Cities themselves are part of the solution, and the article looks at three cities in particular that are facing aging demographics head on--Tokyo, Seoul, and Stockholm.

The article appears in sixth issue of Cities of Opportunity.

headline: Partner, Markets Leader, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Leader, Cyber Risk & Regulatory Private Equity & Transactions, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Member of the Board of Directors
about:
Julie is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 20 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Julie is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Julie ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Julie advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Julie has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Julie has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Julie has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

about:
As a recent MBA graduate from the University of Miami’s Herbert School of Business, I bring a diverse academic and professional background spanning international relations, economics, media production, and business strategy. With dual bachelor’s degrees in ​International Relations​ and ​Economics​ from the University of Iowa and a master’s in ​International Business​, I have honed my analytical, communication, and leadership skills across industries—from media (newspapers, television) to legal services (law firm assistant) and corporate roles (writer, reporter, event planner, and executive support).

My international education and 7 years of experience in the U.S. have equipped me with a global mindset and cross-functional expertise. Now, I am eager to leverage my multidisciplinary knowledge to drive impactful solutions in the business world, aligning my career with my passion for strategic problem-solving and value creation.

​Career Update:​
After returning to China, I began my professional journey at ​PwC Shanghai​, joining the ​Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) Research Team​ in June 2023. Over 1.5 years, I contributed to ​research, consulting, and audit support​, helping clients navigate complex financial landscapes. In October 2024, I transitioned to the ​Risk Assurance – GRC (Governance, Risk & Compliance) team​, where I now focus on ​risk management, internal audit, compliance, and corporate governance​.

At PwC, I am committed to solving critical business challenges and fostering ​trust in society​—whether through robust risk frameworks, strategic insights, or governance excellence. I welcome opportunities to connect with professionals who share a vision for sustainable, ethical, and transformative business practices.

publications.title: Evolving healthcare provider ERM programs
publications.description: PwC conducted research to assess the state of enterprise risk management (ERM) within healthcare providers and found many are operating at comparable levels to their peers. However, given the increasingly complex and risk saturated environment providers operate in, there’s an urgency for providers to continuously enhance and improve their ERM programs beyond their current capabilities.

publications.title: Integrating enterprise risk management and business continuity management
publications.description: Organizations that integrate enterprise risk management (ERM) into their strategic planning efforts have found that business continuity management (BCM) enhances both their value creation objectives and their protection objectives. The confidence that comes from identifying and appropriately addressing interruption risks enables them to more boldly execute those strategic plans. But to gain that confidence requires the melding of ERM and BCM programs.

publications.title: Integration opportunities for ERM programs
publications.description: The best way to sustain enterprise risk management (ERM) programs—and generate ongoing value–is to integrate risk management processes with other business activities. Successful integration efforts require substantial planning and organization buy-in. We believe a comprehensive risk-management-process integration plan can improve risk management information, overall risk culture, and strategic decision making.

publications.title: Steps to Devising a Successful Enterprise Risk Management Program
publications.description: Quoted from my presentation at RIMS ERM Conference in Chicago, October 26th - 27th, 2015   “We see over and over where organizations start out really strong and have executive support, but then they don’t continue to steadily grow the risk management process at their organizations,” said Steve Zawoyski, Minneapolis-based partner and enterprise risk management leader at PwC.

publications.title: Integrating risk scenario analysis into an ERM program
publications.description: This publication describes the potential benefits from risk scenario analysis, and describes a methodology for introducing risk scenario analysis to support strategic decision-making.

publications.title: The evolution of ERM programs
publications.description: A primary goal of enterprise risk management (ERM) programs should be to create a sustainable and value-adding ERM program that can survive management turnover, shifting priorities, and resource challenges. This article describes common risk management program trajectories, common pitfalls, and a methodology and long-term plan for supporting a successful and relevant ERM program.

publications.title: Building a strategic ERM program
publications.description: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) programs that focus on and are consistently aligned with the company’s strategic priorities are likely to provide the greatest benefits to organizations. This article articulates the challenges and provides real examples of how companies have aligned strategies with risk management activities.

publications.title: Why risk assessments fail
publications.description: Risk assessments are a foundational component of risk management programs, but often fail to fully support both program and business objectives. This article identifies the primary reasons for risk assessment fatigue and failure, and ways to improve success.

publications.title: Strategic risk management includes opportunities, not just risk
publications.description: Quoted - "As you go down that maturity, ultimately the goal is you want to include risk in your decision-making process, improving the way you make decisions and the speed at which you can make decisions,” said Steve Zawoyski, a partner at PricewaterhouseCoopers L.L.P. in Minneapolis.

publications.title: From Compliance to ERM
publications.description:
Regulators clearly want corporate boards to embrace the idea of enterprise risk management, and boards are leaning on compliance officers to start that process. This panel will explore how compliance officers can lead that charge, expanding beyond straightforward (if maddening) regulatory compliance to a more forward-looking approach to risk generally.
Featuring:
Peter Agnoletto, Chief Audit Executive and ERM Leader/Senior Director of Internal Audit, Par Pharmaceutical Companies

headline: Partner, Markets Leader, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Leader, Cyber Risk & Regulatory Private Equity & Transactions, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Member of the Board of Directors
about:
Vanessa is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 15 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Vanessa is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Vanessa ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Vanessa advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Vanessa has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Vanessa has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Vanessa has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

headline: Global Structuring-Transfer Pricing Manager, PwC | Board Member | Economic Policy and Development Advocate
about:
I have a diverse experience working on a wide portfolio of projects including value chain transformation, transfer pricing planning, global structuring, and intangible property valuations, in addition to transfer pricing compliance and country-by-country reporting under both the US and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) frameworks. Served multinational companies operating in various jurisdictions around the world and across multiple industries including energy, petrochemicals, pharmaceutical, technology, consumer goods, and nonprofit. 

Prior to joining PwC, I have had the chance to lead the growth of a small local office to one of the highest-profile operation centers in the region. I devised creative strategies and business operations that created sustainable value and provided solutions to challenges that stunted the development of new businesses in the region and particularly hindered small manufacturers and startups. 

Other than transfer pricing and strategic management, I am passionate about language learning and international development. I currently speak three languages (Arabic, French, and English) and I am learning three more. I led and engaged in different initiatives focused on economic policy, systems change, and capacity building around the world. I was elected as one of the Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom (WILPF) US delegates to discuss challenges and opportunities for the empowerment of rural women at the Commission on the Status of Women review meetings at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, and participated in different discussions and summits held in collaboration with the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and World Centre for Sustainable Development among others.

headline: Partner, Markets Leader, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Leader, Cyber Risk & Regulatory Private Equity & Transactions, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Member of the Board of Directors
about:
Emily is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 15 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Emily is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Emily ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Emily advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Emily has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Emily has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Emily has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

about:
Diana is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 20 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Diana is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Diana ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Diana advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Diana has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Diana has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Diana has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

about:
Joe Wiggins is an trust solutions assurance partner with PwC. He has over 30 years of experience specializing in financial services, and currently serves as the Global Alternative Funds Practice Leader for PwC. Prior to moving to Chicago in 2010, Joe spent most of his career working in the firm’s New York Asset and Wealth Management Practice.  Joe returned to New York in October 2021 to become one of the US Asset and Wealth Management team practice leaders.  He has extensive experience in investment fund audits with a particular focus on annual financial statement audits for non-registered and registered investment products, including private equity, hedge funds and investment companies. 

Joe has served many multi-billion dollar hedge fund firms with strategies including credit derivatives, macro, relative value and RMBS as well as currently serving several firms in the Chicago marketplace. In the private equity area, Joe's clients have included a major financial institution with more than 70 private equity funds and in excess of $6 billion of invested capital in middle-market buyouts, as well as growth equity and venture capital in the United States, Europe and Asia. Joe has also been one of the audit partners serving one of the world's leading private investment firms with approximately $25 billion under management in funds and accounts. Additionally, Joe was the engagement partner for a large 100+ registered investment fund complex of a major insurance company. 

Joe led the National Learning and Education program for the U.S. Asset and Wealth Management practice from 2003 to 2010. He is a frequent presenter at industry events, as well as PwC sponsored conferences. He served as a Board member of the Midwest Chapter of Hedge Fund Cares charity organization from 2010 to 2021 and a Board member and Treasurer for the Managed Funds Association from 2018-2021 and was an active partner champion of PwC's diversity, equality and inclusion efforts through the PwC Diversity Council for Chicago. Joe earned a Bachelor of Business Administration in accounting at the University of Iowa, and is a member of several CPA state societies as well as the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

projects.title: Crisis Communications Plan (severe snowfall at the Chicago Department of Streets and Sanitation)
projects.description:
An assignment for my Crisis Communications class during my senior year at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. We were assigned a company or organization — mine was the City of Chicago's Department of Streets and Sanitation — and had to come up with a plan in the event of a plausible crisis.
I focused my project on the crisis of "severe snowfall." I had to research the leaders of the department, as well as local news outlets and local emergency personnel that we would need to communicate with in the event of the crisis. I also gathered information on the city's snow/ice removal process and services and other tools (such as apps or notification systems) that may be of service to residents of Chicago in the event of the crisis.
As the "Crisis Communications Manager" I also created a fill-in-the-blanks news release to be used in the event of an "extreme snowfall incident" and created a list of "key messages" to share with employees so everyone is on the same page when talking to residents and/or the press.

headline: Catedrática, Full Professor of Econometrics at UAM, Director of the ECONRES research group. Fellow of the Regional Studies Association (FeRSA). Member of the Editorial Board of Journal of Geographical Systems.
about: Coro Chasco is "Catedrática" (full professor) of Applied Economics. She earned her PhD and graduated with honors in Applied Economic Modelling at UAM. She is Fellow of the Regional Studies Association (FeRSA), since 2022, as well as invited professor in the University of Santiago de Chile (since 2019) and University Rey Juan Carlos University, Madrid (since 2016). She was also visiting scholar in the University of Chicago (2017, 2018), Adolfo Ibáñez University, Chile (2014) and University of Illinois (2004), and visiting professor of the University of Franche-Comté, France (2013-2014). She is member of the editorial board of several journals like Journal of Geographical Systems. She was co-editor of the Journal Spatial Economic Analysis (2020-2023), among others. She directs the ECONRES research group and works in spatial econometrics and spatial statistics with applications to regional inequalities, housing prices, environment, tourism and quality of life. She is highly experienced in the generation of statistics on micro-territorial variables.

projects.title: Specification Searches in Spatial Econometric Models. Method and Practice (3SEM)
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
projects.description:
This project builds on the two main features of spatial econometrics, interdependence and heterogeneity, to which we add instability. We focus on the topics of uncertainty in the weights matrix and on the problem of changing regimes. Our framework are panel or pseudo-panel data models. In essence, this a methodological project with a strong applied research program. The weight matrix is a key element in the construction of an spatial model. Its specification follows from an a priori decision. This situation has begun to change in recent years, with more formal procedures. Our contribution sets out two lines of research. In first place, we want to elaborate an strategy to select the optimal weight matrix from among a finite group of matrices. Then we develop methods to detect when, using panel information, a change in the weights matrix has occurred. This result is necessary to tackle a more ambitious objective, the modeling of the weights matrix which should be estimated from the data. Regime changes mirror the instability of spatial relationships. In the past we have worked in that problem trying to detect breaks; our interest now is on modeling the breaks using two approaches: a discrete procedure based on Stat-Scan and a continuous one using STAR models. The first will be useful to differentiate between spatial dependence and groupwise heteroskedasticity, and also among different types of spatial dependence. STAR models have been recently introduced in a spatial context and our objective is to extend their use also to the mechanisms of spatial dependence. The purpose is to get rid of the restriction of symmetry, introducing higher nonlinearities in this kind of models.

Government of Spain for the project entitled "Specification Searches in Spatial Econometric Models. Method and Practice (3SEM)” (ref.: ECO2015-65758-P). Principal Investigator: Jesús Mur and Ana Angulo (University of Zaragoza, Spain).

projects.title: Atlas Socieconómico de Extremadura 2017
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
projects.description:
Con este IV Atlas Socioeconómico de Extremadura se consolida una publicación a todas luces necesaria para conocer con el mayor detalle posible cada uno de los 388 pueblos y ciudades de la región. Se trata de un compendio minucioso que suministra información muy diversa y valiosa que permite, sin duda, extraer conclusiones sobre los potenciales escenarios de desarrollo y de futuro de nuestra tierra.
Esta nueva edición incorpora, además de la actualización temporal de las series de datos ya presentadas en ocasiones anteriores, información de la deuda municipal, indice de actividad empresarial, análisis migratorio de Extremadura, tiempo de viaje a la cabecera de área e indicadores de emprendimiento sectorial.
El Atlas comprende nueve capítulos claramente diferenciados y que se refieren a Indicadores Económicos, Demográficos y Sociales; Áreas Comerciales; Indicadores de Emprendimiento; Evolución de Indicadores Estadísticos; Caracterización Sociodemográfica por distritos de los municipios más importantes; Indicadores Básicos de las Mancomunidades de Extremadura y Anexo de mapas temáticos. Se trata, por tanto, de un trabajo exhaustivo que año tras año va ganando en riqueza y en interés y que incluye estadísticas que se colocan, cada vez más, en el epicentro de los debates sociales y políticos.

projects.associatedWith: Associated with Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
projects.description:
National figures alone cannot reveal the full and sometimes complex picture of what is happening at a more detailed level within the European Union (EU). In this respect, statistical information at a subnational level is an important tool for highlighting specific regional and territorial aspects. It helps in analysing changing patterns and the impact that policy decisions can have on our daily life. In order to provide a detailed picture of the diverse EU territories and to monitor EU regional policy targets, Eurostat has developed a range of statistics based on different classifications and typologies. These include data for: regions, cities and greater cities, metropolitan regions, rural areas and regions.
Specific geographies such as coastal regions, mountain regions, border regions or island regions are also covered.

El primero se centra en aspectos sociales mientras que el segundo contiene indicadores económicos. En ambos casos, el Centro Gauss del Instituto Lawrence R. Klein, de la Universidad Autónoma de Madrid ha sido el encargado de preparar la amplia base de datos. Con la publicación de este anuario, la Fundación “la Caixa” pretende facilitar tanto el trabajo de los investigadores profesionales de las ciencias sociales como la consulta por parte de otros colectivos y del público en general. Con este objetivo, año tras año se ha ido mejorando y completando el contenido del anuario, tanto en la versión impresa del mismo como en la electrónica, que incluso ofrece mayores desgloses de algunas variables y amplía las posibilidades de búsqueda y tratamiento de los datos. 
En esta edición, se ofrecen más de 100 variables nuevas. Entre las principales novedades, cabe destacar: el nivel de instrucción de la población (personas analfabetas y sin estudios, con estudios primarios, secundarios o universitarios), el estado civil de la población (solteros, casados, viudos, separados y divorciados), la composición de hogares y viviendas (número de miembros por hogar, régimen de tenencia de la vivienda y hogares con disponibilidad de segunda vivienda) y la población de riesgo para la salud (fumadores, consumidores de alcohol, sedentarios y personas obesas o con sobrepeso).

publications.title: Probit Models for Grouped-data Migration Flows: A Theoretical Note
publications.description: In this theoretical note, we propose the GProbit model as an alternative to gravity models to estimate grouped-data flows. This is a model based on the random utility theory, which is consistent with the principle of population behavior. Instead of migrant counts, the dependent variable of the GProbit model of flows consists of a number of observed proportions. It allows explaining the propensity to migrate from any origin to a destination, which is an interesting relative concept not affected by the size effect. For this reason, it is expected to have better fit and less problems of non-normality, as illustrated by an application for the internal migration flows of the Spanish regions.

publications.title: A scan test for spatial groupwise heteroscedasticity in cross-sectional models with an application on houses prices in Madrid
publications.publishedAt: Regional Science and Urban Economics 68 · Jan 1, 2018
publications.description: We propose a scan test for the presence of spatial groupwise heteroskedasticity in cross-sectional data. The scan approach has been used in different fields before, including spatial econometric models, to detect instability in mean values of variables or regression residuals. In this paper, we extend its use to second order moments. Using large Monte Carlo simulations, we check the reliability of the proposed scan procedure to detect instabilities in the variance, the size and power of the test and its accuracy to find spatial clusters of observations with similar variances. Finally, we illustrate the usefulness of this test to improve the specification search in a spatial hedonic model, with an empirical application on housing prices in Madrid.

publications.title: Spatial contagion of civil liberty: some evidence from a spatial econometrics analysis
publications.description: This paper focuses on civil liberty, which is defined as the individual right to make decisions without interference within a given vital space. It studies the principal factors conditioning civil liberty, one of them being the spatial contagion among neighboring countries. To this purpose, we employ the Civil Liberty Gastil index from Freedom House in a spatial autoregressive  (SAR)  model  estimated  from  a  sample  of  175  coun-tries for the year 2010. The results provide good evidence for spatial contagion (spillover effects) of civil liberty across the world. Countries “catch” around 30% of the average changes in their neighbors’ civil liberty levels. Additionally we have also identified religious culture and the Internet as other important variables explaining the differing levels of civil liberty among the world’s countries.

publications.title: Determinants of trust towards tourist destinations
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Destination Marketing & Management 6(4) · Dec 1, 2017
publications.description: Trust has become a relevant concern for tourist destinations. Partly because of the novelty of the research on trust in the tourism literature, there are several open questions regarding the antecedents of trust towards a tourist destination. In this research, we suggest that reputation, and cognitive and affective evaluation of a destination, are relevant antecedents of trust. Trust towards a tourist destination is understood as a multidimensional construct, including local inhabitants and public and private institutions that are honest, benevolent and competent. This paper used a non-probabilistic sample of 750 tourists based on quotas, proportionally distributed among the main tourist destinations in Chile. After testing the psychometric properties of the scales developed for this study, a structural equation model was estimated and it was found that trust is a consequence of the reputation of the destination, as well as the cognitive and affective evaluation of the tourists. The paper concludes by emphasising the importance of these findings for the tourism industry, and outlines recommendations to reinforce trust relations with tourists.

publications.title: n honor of Geoffrey Hewings
publications.description: This special issue contains a selection of many excellent papers and posters presented at the Sixth ‘Jean Paelinck’ Seminar of Spatial Econometrics, which was held at the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM) in October, 2013. The collection of papers address some of the major concerns and progression lines proposed by professor Paelinck along his academic life for spatial econometrics: the treatment of spatial data and the need to specify and estimate appropriate econometric models in the realm of regional and urban science. The first two papers in this issue present two methods to detect spatial clusters (Rodero-Cosano, Salinas-Pérez, García-Alonso and Salvador-Carulla) and concentrations (Thomas-Agnan and Bonneu) using homogeneous micro-data and individual observations, respectively, to adequately deal with the Modifiable Areal Unit Problem. The following three articles focus on the specification of spatial effects –spatial autocorrelation and spatial heterogeneity– in more complex situations. Le Gallo and Chasco propose a nonparametric approach to deal with spatial effects when the model’s parametric structure is unknown, as it is the case in hedonic models with large databases. Ezcurra and Ríos derive a spatial Durbin panel data model from theory in order to model the spatio-temporal relationship between output volatily and regional growth. Finally, Díaz-Lanchas, Gallego, Llano and De la Mata take into account spatial complexity in trade flows introducing spatial dependence in a gravity model.

publications.title: Entrepreneurship at regional level: Temporary and neighborhood effects
publications.description: This paper analyzes the spatial nature of entrepreneurship at NUTSIII. Lately, academic studies are including the relation between incipient entrepreneurs and geography. In some cases, this relation is considered as unidirectional insofar as the decision to become an entrepreneur can be highly influenced by geographical location. Beyond the cultural and social boundaries that affect the entrepreneur as an individual, there are spatial characteristics that provide advantages of location for some industries. While several studies highlight the role of location and geography as aspects that have an impact on entrepreneurial activity, the externalities generated by such aspects are not considered in empirical work. The aim of this paper is to check how avoiding considering location can have an effect on the results of entrepreneurship research. Our results point that both location and temporary effects have a significant impact on entrepreneurship research results. Thus, it is important to use a temporary and spatial methodological approach in entrepreneurship research to avoid bias.

publications.title: Identifying local determinants of destination choices of international immigrants to the Madrid Metropolitan Area
publications.description: We examine the local determinants of destination choices of foreign immigrants to the Madrid metro area using data for 2005 and 2009 from the Spanish annual municipal-level registers of inhabitants. Taking advantage of the equivalence relation between conditional logit and Poisson, we estimate a location-choice model using the Poisson fixed-effects estimator. Origin-destination fixed effects are incorporated to account for the persistent spatial structure of the immigrants’ settlement patterns and to control for potential violations of the independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA) assumption. The Poisson regression model is estimated for seven different groups of immigrants according to world regions or countries of origin. Our modelling strategy has important empirical implications, with magnitudes and/or signs of the estimated coefficients changing in the expected directions. It is found that newly arriving immigrants tend to settle in low-to-middle-income locations in the suburban reaches of the Madrid metro area. Moreover, the effects of the size of local communities of established immigrants are found to be insignificant and even negative in several instances, reflecting hetero-local settlement preferences and/or the saturation of local networks causing in-group job rivalry, respectively.

publications.title: Long-run determinants of economic growth in South America
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Applied Economics XIX(1) · May 1, 2016
publications.description: Based on an annual historical database for South American countries from 1960 to 2008, we develop an empirical study to gain insight into the long-run determinants of economic growth using a two-equation framework. A system of two panel data models is estimated to identify the growth determinants and their connection with foreign direct investment. We find that economic growth is driven most strongly by physical and human capital accumulation, as well as by sectorial exports, and that institutions and policy have a substantial impact on economic growth and investment. Macroeconomic disturbances have a significant detrimental effect on long-run growth. Trade openness correlates positively with foreign investment, indicating that relatively closed countries stand to benefit most from opening up their economies. Our division of the sample into two sub-periods, 1960–1980 and 1981–2008, indicates a structural change.

publications.title: Heterogeneity in perceptions of noise and air pollution: A spatial quantile approach on the city of Madrid
publications.description: In this paper, we apply a hedonic housing price model to estimate the willingness to pay for less air pollution and noise in the city of Madrid. Using subjective data on the perception of air pollution and noise by the Madrid residents, we apply a quantile conditionally parametric model that allows one to quantify the heterogeneity of this willingness to pay values across quantiles of the conditional distributions of housing prices and their spatial heterogeneity across the whole study area. The results show that implicit prices for clean and quiet environment differ substantially across the housing markets, depending on the perceived intensity of pollution, accessibility to jobs and leisure, and some socioeconomic characteristics of the population. In particular, in some areas, households seem to make a trade-off between improvements in communication and some worsening in environmental conditions.

publications.title: Exploring Scan methods to test spatial structure with an application to housing prices in Madrid
publications.description: We evaluate the usefulness of the spatial scan test in specification testing for spatial econometric models. The null hypothesis assumes equality of the mean values of a variable in all the locations of a geo‐referenced data set. The alternative hypothesis relies on the existence of one (or more) spatial cluster(s) where mean values differ from those of the rest of the sample. First, we conduct a Monte‐Carlo simulation study to analyse the properties of this test when applied to regression residuals. Second, we illustrate this test with an empirical application on housing prices in Madrid.

publications.title: A comparative analysis of the effect of aid and microfinance on growth
publications.publishedAt: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d’études du développement 36 · Jan 23, 2015
publications.description: This paper investigates the effect of official development aid (ODA) and microfinance (MF) on economic growth and compares the results. We identify and analyse the transmission mechanisms from ODA and microfinance to growth. We then study the effects of ODA and microfinance on growth, using an unbalanced panel of 67 countries for the period 2001–2011. Accounting for country and time effects, our results show that microfinance has a positive and statistically significant effect on economic growth through private investment, while ODA has no effect on growth. This suggests that deploying resources in the microfinance industry will foster economic development in poor countries.

publications.title: Objective index of quality of life in Spain
publications.publishedAt: Encyclopaedia of Quality of Life and Well-Being Research. Springer · Jan 1, 2014
publications.description: Quality of life is a complex concept involving various socioeconomic domains, some of which can be measured objectively (e.g., income level, access to health services, educational level) whereas others are more a matter of people’s subjective evaluations of happiness, health, or social relationships. The 1991 Nobel Laureate Amartya Sen defines social welfare as a multidimensional concept that should not be limited to disposable income but should include other targets like education, security, health, and even personal wishes. The Spanish National Statistics Institute similarly defines welfare as the state of equal opportunities in which everyone enjoys access to all “socially desirable” tangible and intangible resources (INE, 2011).

publications.title: GeoDaSpace: a resource for teaching spatial regression models
publications.description: Spatial econometrics has become a prominent topic in the recent scientific literature. For this reason, it is being used in research as well as teaching both undergraduate and graduate econometrics courses. GeoDaSpace is a software package for the estimation and testing of spatial econometric models in an intuitive and easy-to-use point and click environment. It is still an alpha release freely downloadable from the GeoDa Center (Arizona State University), which incorporates a wide range of estimation methods (OLS, 2SLS, ML, GM/GMM) and models (spatial lag, spatial error, spatial lag and error, spatial regimes), with options for spatial and non-spatial diagnostics, non-spatial endogenous variables and heteroskedasticity/HAC covariance estimators. GeoDaSpace is a very useful teaching resource that can be used by both teachers and students.

publications.title: The impact of objective and subjective measures of air quality and noise on house prices: A multilevel approach for downtown Madrid
publications.description: Air quality and urban noise are major concerns in big cities. This article presents an evaluation of how they affect transaction prices in downtown Madrid. For this purpose, we incorporated both objective and subjective measures of air quality and noise and used multilevel models, since our sample was hierarchically organized into three levels: 5,080 houses (level 1) in 759 census tracts (level 2) and 43 neighborhoods (level 3). Variables are available for each level, individual characteristics for the first level, and various socioeconomic data for the other levels. We estimated multilevel hedonic models to assess the marginal willingness to pay for better air quality and reduced noise in downtown Madrid. We found that noise and air pollution are place‐based perception variables with a so‐called halo effect: residents in wealthier neighborhoods do not perceive their environment as being highly polluted because of their higher “sense of place.” In addition, we found a counterintuitive positive sign for the effect of objective measures of pollutants on housing prices but a significantly negative effect of the subjective measures. For these reasons, we conclude that housing prices are better explained by subjective evaluation factors than by objective measurements.

publications.title: Hierarchy and spatial autocorrelation effects in hedonic models
publications.description: Hedonic housing price models should deal with spatial autocorrelation in order to avoid bias and inconsistency in the coefficient estimates. Multilevel models have been presented as a way of properly considering the effects of neighbourhood amenities operating at different spatial hierarchies. In this paper, we test this feature by specifying a three-level model for a dataset on downtown Madrid, which includes spatially lagged explanatory variables. The results show that hierarchical models are not capable of fully capturing spatial autocorrelation so that more effort should be done in developing the appropriate spatial multilevel models.

publications.title: The influence of geography on the spatial agglomeration of production in the European Union
publications.description: We investigate the relative impact of geographic features on the location of production in the European Union. Specifically, we attempt to quantify how much of the spatial pattern of GDP can be attributed to exogenous first-nature elements alone and how much can be derived from endogenous second-nature factors. In order to disentangle both effects empirically, we control for second-nature factors. A method based on the decomposition of the per capita GDP variance is applied to a panel of 1,171 European NUTS 3 regions for 2006. We demonstrate that variable and model misspecifications may bias results unless proper allowance is made for spatial autocorrelation and spatial heterogeneity, as well as multicollinearity and endogeneity.

publications.title: Dealing with data at various spatial scales and supports: An application on traffic noise and air pollution effects on housing prices with multilevel models
publications.publishedAt: Defining the Spatial Scale in Modern Regional Analysis. Springer · Jan 1, 2012
publications.description: In empirical studies dealing with spatial data, researchers are frequently confronted with data available at different spatial scales. For instance, hedonic models on housing prices usually combine individual data pertaining to the price and structural characteristics of the dwelling and socio-economic neighbourhood characteristics that are available at some upper administrative levels. Another frequent issue is the change of support problem or misaligned regression problem (Gotway and Young 2002; Banerjee et al. 2004) when there is a spatial mismatch between the spatial supports of the variables. For instance, the measurement of air quality is based on regular sampling at a few stations in an area whereas socio-economic data are available for aggregate administrative.

publications.title: Building an environmental quality index for a big city: a spatial interpolation approach combined with a distance indicator
publications.description: One of the main tasks of regional and environmental economics is to construct Environmental Quality Indexes for big cities. A standard method is to generate a single measure as a linear combination of several contaminants by applying Principal Component Analysis. Spatial interpolation is then carried out to determine pollution levels across the city. We innovate on this method and propose an alternative approach. First, we combine a set of noise and air pollutants measured at a number of monitoring stations with data available for each census tract. This yields a mixed environmental index that is socioeconomically more complete. We then apply kriging to match the monitoring station records to the census data. Finally, we construct a composite pollution index using the Pena Distance method (DP2), which proves more robust than traditional approaches.

publications.title: Multilevel models: an application to the beta-convergence model, Région et Développement 30
publications.publishedAt: Multilevel models: an application to the beta-convergence model, Région et Développement 30 · Jan 1, 2009
publications.description: Many kinds of data in the social sciences have a hierarchical, multilevel or clustered structure. For example, municipalities are grouped into regions; regions are formed within countries; and quite often, countries belong to supra-national organizations. Once groupings are established, they will tend to become differentiated, and this differentiation implies that the group and its members both influence and are influenced by group membership. To ignore this relationship is to risk overlooking the importance of group effects and it may also render invalid many of the traditional statistical analysis techniques used for studying data relationships. In this paper, we specify a basic two-level model for a conditional beta-convergence model of a sample of European NUTS-2 regions. Specifically, we test for the role of regional decentralization (country-level variable) on regional income growth, since it has been suggested that countries with a governmental form of regional decentralization foster innovation and economic growth.

publications.title: Spatial analysis of urban growth in Spain, 1900-2001
publications.description: The purpose of this paper is to improve the knowledge of the Spanish urban system. We study the evolution of population growth among the group of 722 municipalities included in the Spanish urban areas over the period 1900–2001. A spatial SUR model is estimated for Zipf’s law and shows the existence of two main phases: divergence (1900–1980) and convergence (1980–2001). Then, the cross-sectional distribution of urban population is characterized by means of nonparametric estimations of density functions and the growth process is modeled as a first-order stationary Markov chain. Spatial effects are finally introduced within the Markov chain framework using regional conditioning. This analysis shows a low interclass mobility, i.e., a high-persistence of urban municipalities to stay in their own class from one decade to another over the whole period, and the influence of the geographical environment on urban population dynamism.

publications.title: Ecological inference and spatial heterogeneity: an entropy‐based distributionally weighted regression approach
publications.description: In this article we compare two competing approaches to ecological modelling using test data. The first approach is based on the “traditional” method of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), assuming constancy of parameters across disaggregated spatial units (spatial homogeneity). The second (new) approach is based on the method of Generalised Cross‐Entropy (GCE), assuming varying parameters (spatial heterogeneity). The latter approach is designated as entropy‐based “distributionally weighted regression” (DWR). The two approaches are tested in a real‐world application, using data on per‐capita GDP for the 17 regions and some covariates for the 50 provinces of Spain. Specifically, the performances of the two approaches are assessed by examining their capability in tracking the actual per‐capita GDP data for the provinces (while treating them as if they were not observed by the econometrician), and in showing evidence of spatial heterogeneity. Our findings indicate that the GCE varying‐parameter approach outperforms the OLS approach in terms of predictive power. Specifically, we find that the GCE predictions make efficient use of the lower‐level information that is available. In addition, it is shown that entropy‐based DWR has some potential as a useful technique for investigating spatially heterogeneous relationships at the lower level of analysis that might otherwise be overlooked.

publications.title: Econometría espacial aplicada a la predicción- extrapolación de datos microterritoriales
publications.publishedAt: Comunidad de Madrid, Consejería de Economía e Innovación Tecnológica, Madrid · Apr 1, 2003
publications.description: Este estudio contribuye a una mayor profundicación tanto en el campo científico de la econometría, como, en general, en las ciencias sociales, con una especial trascendencia para la economía de la Comunidad de Madrid. En lo que se refiere al ámbito científico, se propone la predicción-extrapolación de datos microterritoriales como parte de la econometría espacial, presentando una metodología fundamentada en instrumentos exploratorios y confirmatorios propios de esta ciencia. La predicción-extrapolación de datos geográficos podría definirse como el conjunto de métodos inferenciales destinados a obtener datos microterritoriales, no disponibles, a partir de información espacial agregada proporcionada por fuentes oficiales. Para ello, se realiza una revisión completa y clara de los principios básicos de la econometría espacial, una disciplina no bien conocida con la suficiente profundidad en España, con la excepción de algunos investigadores. Esta obra constituye también una importante contribución al análisis económico en cuanto que acomete la estimación de un importante indicador de bienestar social, la renta familiar disponible, a un nivel espacial microterritorial municipal. Pero la trascendencia de este estudio se extiende, en general, a las ciencias sociales, dado que el proceso de predicción-extrapolación espacial, en cuanto obtención de datos espaciales no disponibles en una escala geográfica inferior, supera el ámbito del análisis económico y abarcaría también temas como la ciencia política, sociología, marketing u otros campos de aplicación, como la sanidad.

She has demonstrated the ability to lead cross functional teams to high levels of success in a variety of competitive, innovative markets and fast paced global environments.
 She is a collaborative and transformative leader who can shape business goals into strategic initiatives, to achieve strong financial results.

headline: Clinical Assistant Professor at Gies College of Business - University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Independent Director, Retired Partner - PwC
about:
Highly-technical expert. Transformational advisor.  Empowering mentor. These are the roles I thrive in and the qualities that have allowed me to generate trust and achieve success among the organizations I have supported through more than three decades of my career. 

As a Partner, CPA and senior-level accounting and financial reporting professional, I have progressed through various roles in audit oversight, client management, team development, business group start-up and educator. If one constant has remained intact through the years, it is this: I am a go-to “change agent”—entrusted to advise, facilitate and direct through periods of volatility and transformation.  My goal is always to ensure that the organizations and clients I represent feel encouraged to have me in their corner. I take great pride in my ongoing development of successes devising solutions, driving initiatives, improving processes, and enhancing employee and client experiences. 

I believe my most significant contributions as an executive leader are derived from experiences I’ve had working and living internationally. I have gained cross-cultural understanding and sensitivity for the various nuances that exist in the financial and business world as well as among various groups of people.  This has not only been essential to the expansion of my professional expertise, but also vital to an effective, open leadership approach. I operate under a very open-minded perspective that allows me to genuinely identify and thoughtfully communicate with my team, recognize individual potential, and foster career enhancement.  

I look forward to further applying my breadth of experience and passion for company, industry, team and personal development.
